- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction of -1–2% for 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 60–70-day trend); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 5–10 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the “late-cycle” peak (last 5–7 days of forecast horizon); adjust upward by 0.5–2% if sentiment is bullish and price has been trending upward for 10+ days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% bias toward the sentiment direction for next 3–7 days.
